entries.sense_en: before long; in a short while

synonyms.nuance: Formal and common in announcements; a short time from now.
The everyday word; presently sounds more formal and old-fashioned.
Means 'now', not 'soon'. American speakers use presently this way too, so context matters.

entries.tip_ko: 특히 미국 영어에서는 '현재'라는 뜻으로도 쓰이지만, 이 글에서는 '곧'이라는 뜻이에요.

entries.sense_en: to accept someone or something annoying without complaining

synonyms.nuance: More formal; accepting something you do not like, without implying real suffering.
synonyms.example: The school does not tolerate bullying.

synonyms.nuance: Stronger; suffering something painful or difficult over a long time.
Informal; usually negative ('I can't stand him'), about what you cannot bear.

entries.tip_ko: put up with 뒤에는 사람이나 사물이 바로 옵니다: put up with the noise.

entries.sense_en: calm and confident, in control of yourself even in an awkward situation

synonyms.nuance: Calm and controlled, often after or despite stress; less about confidence.
synonyms.example: She stayed composed during the interview.

synonyms.nuance: Graceful as well as calm; suggests elegant, balanced manners.
Broader: believing in your own ability; does not imply calm manners.
synonyms.example: He felt confident about the test.

entries.sense_en: tried hard to do something

synonyms.nuance: The plain everyday word; no sense of effort or formality.
Suggests long, determined effort toward a goal.
Neutral and formal; focuses on the try, which may fail.
synonyms.example: He attempted to climb the wall.

entries.tip_ko: 영국식 철자 endeavour, 미국식은 endeavor입니다. 뒤에 to + 동사가 옵니다.

entries.sense_en: in the proper or expected way

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word for 'in the right way'; does not suggest duty or convention.
Fitting for the situation; stresses suitability.
Stresses that something is correct or justified.

entries.tip_ko: formal한 글에서 'duly noted', 'duly paid'처럼 자주 나옵니다. due에서 e가 빠진 철자(duly)에 주의하세요.

entries.sense_en: to move to another place to live; here used a little grandly for moving to the country for a rest cure

synonyms.nuance: The everyday word; any change of home, big or small.
synonyms.example: We moved to Busan last year.

synonyms.nuance: Business-like; often for a job or company.
Leaving your own country for good.

entries.tip_ko: 철새·동물의 이동이나 사람들의 대규모 이주에 흔히 쓰는 말이라, 한 사람이 시골로 내려가는 데 쓰면 약간 거창한 느낌이 납니다.

entries.sense_en: spending time feeling sad and sorry for yourself, doing nothing

synonyms.nuance: Thinking deeply and unhappily about something, often with anger or worry.
Silent bad temper because you are annoyed at someone.
synonyms.example: The child sulked in his room.

synonyms.nuance: Longing sadly for someone or something you miss.

entries.tip_ko: mope around(어슬렁거리며 시무룩하게 지내다)의 형태로도 자주 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: a quiet place where you go to rest and get away from busy life

synonyms.nuance: A place of safety from danger or trouble, not just quiet.
synonyms.example: The cave was a refuge from the storm.

synonyms.nuance: Secret or private place, often small and cosy.
Holy or protected place; strong sense of safety and peace.

entries.sense_en: swallowed up completely and covered

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word; take something completely inside, often quickly.
Fill or cover with water or too much of something.
synonyms.example: The boat was swamped by waves.

synonyms.nuance: Overpower with force or feeling; often figurative.

entries.tip_ko: 불길·파도·감정 등이 '집어삼키다'라는 강한 표현입니다.

entries.sense_en: looking safe but actually very dangerous
entries.sense_ko: 겉보기엔 안전하지만 위험한, 믿을 수 없는

synonyms.nuance: General word; danger may be obvious. Treacherous hides its danger.
Plain, mild; not protected from harm.
Literary; full of great danger and risk.

entries.tip_ko: 사람에게 쓰면 '배신하는'이라는 뜻이고, 길·날씨·바다에 쓰면 '겉은 멀쩡하나 위험한'이라는 뜻입니다.

entries.sense_en: soft, wet ground that a person can sink into

synonyms.nuance: Wet grassland, often near water; usually easier to walk through than a bog.
Wetland with standing water and trees or bushes.
Soft, boggy ground that sucks you in; also used figuratively for a hopeless situation.

entries.tip_ko: 영국 속어로 화장실을 뜻하기도 하지만 여기서는 '늪'입니다.

entries.sense_en: in a weak, unsteady way, with pauses

synonyms.nuance: Slowly because unsure what to do or say.
With many stops and starts; close to faltering.
Shaky in movement or voice, from weakness or emotion.
synonyms.example: He walked unsteadily to the door.

entries.sense_en: to annoy or irritate someone, often by something done again and again

synonyms.nuance: General word; mild to moderate irritation.
Slightly more formal; also used for skin or throat.
Informal and stronger; makes you nearly crazy.
synonyms.example: The constant noise drives me up the wall.

entries.tip_ko: nerves는 복수형으로 씁니다. 같은 글의 'nerve cure'(신경 쇠약 치료)와 연결해서 기억하세요.

entries.sense_en: to stop speaking suddenly, in the middle of a sentence

synonyms.nuance: Plain word; does not suggest a sudden halt in the middle.
Voice slowly fades away instead of stopping suddenly.
Someone or something ends it before its natural end.

entries.tip_ko: break off은 '뚝 끊다'라는 느낌이고, 관계나 협상을 '끝내다'라는 뜻으로도 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: moved in a quick, busy, energetic way

synonyms.nuance: Move fast because of little time; no sense of busy energy.
Faster and more hurried, sometimes careless.
synonyms.example: He rushed out of the room.

synonyms.nuance: Push forward energetically; informal and often American.

entries.tip_ko: bustle in / bustle about처럼 방향 부사와 함께 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: in a quick, lively, businesslike way

synonyms.nuance: Only speed; nothing about energy or manner.
Stresses effort and vigour rather than a crisp, efficient manner.
Right on time or without delay.

entries.tip_ko: brisk walk(활기찬 걷기), brisk wind(상쾌하게 부는 바람)도 함께 알아 두세요.

entries.sense_en: to talk continuously and quickly, without much thought or interest in the listener

synonyms.nuance: Fast, light talk, often about unimportant things.
synonyms.example: The kids chattered all the way home.

synonyms.nuance: Talk at length, wandering from topic to topic.
synonyms.example: He rambled on about his trip.

synonyms.nuance: Plain phrase; talk for too long, often annoyingly.
synonyms.example: She went on and on about her cat.

entries.tip_ko: rattled(당황한)와는 뜻이 다릅니다. rattle on은 '수다를 떨다'입니다.

entries.sense_en: causing horror; shockingly terrible (here, about the men's deaths)

synonyms.nuance: General word for very unpleasant; not necessarily about death.
Disgusting because of blood, injury or death.
Serious, gloomy and depressing; less shocking.

entries.tip_ko: 철자의 gh는 ghost의 영향을 받은 것입니다. 영국식 구어에서는 '아주 나쁜'이라는 가벼운 표현으로도 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: a weakness or illness of the body, especially a lasting one

synonyms.nuance: A minor or ordinary illness; lighter than infirmity.
Everyday word for being sick; could be short or serious.
Weakness of body from age or delicate health.

entries.tip_ko: infirm(노쇠한)의 명사형입니다. 격식 있는 글에서 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 잘 안 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: a false belief that someone holds firmly, even against the evidence

synonyms.nuance: A false idea or appearance; may be pleasant and known to be false.
A wrong idea from misunderstanding; milder, correctable with facts.
Imagined thing; may be enjoyed knowingly.
synonyms.example: a fantasy of winning the lottery

entries.tip_ko: delusion은 사실을 알려 줘도 안 바뀌는 강한 착각(의학 용어로는 '망상')이지만, 여기서는 Framton의 흔한 착각을 비꼬는 가벼운 표현입니다.

entries.sense_en: shocked and unable to think or react clearly

synonyms.nuance: Shocked into silence or stillness, often by news.
synonyms.example: She was stunned by the result.

synonyms.nuance: Unable to understand; no sense of shock.
synonyms.example: I was confused by the map.

synonyms.nuance: Unable to feel emotion after shock or grief.
synonyms.example: He felt numb after the news.

entries.sense_en: the time in the evening when light is fading and it is almost dark

synonyms.nuance: The soft light itself, just after sunset; slightly more poetic.
The moment night arrives; darker than dusk.
The moment the sun goes down; earlier than dusk.

entries.tip_ko: dawn(새벽)과 짝으로 기억하세요: dawn은 아침, dusk는 저녁입니다.

entries.sense_en: rough and dry, as a voice after shouting or a sore throat

synonyms.nuance: Low and slightly rough, often attractively so.
Rough and unfriendly in manner or tone.
Informal; like a frog, usually because of a cold.

entries.tip_ko: horse(말)와 발음이 같습니다 (/hɔrs/).

entries.sense_en: very fast and without stopping to think

synonyms.nuance: Done too quickly without enough care.
Ignoring danger; stresses risk more than speed.
Done in a hurry; neutral, no sense of panic.

entries.tip_ko: 원래 '머리부터 (head first)'라는 뜻에서 왔습니다. 부사로도 씁니다: fall headlong.

entries.sense_en: ran away suddenly and very fast

synonyms.nuance: Run quickly for a short distance; not necessarily out of fear.
synonyms.example: She dashed to the bus stop.

synonyms.nuance: Formal; run away from danger.
British slang; run off to avoid trouble.
synonyms.example: The boys scarpered when the police came.

entries.tip_ko: bolt은 '볼트, 빗장'이라는 뜻도 있지만, 여기서는 말이 놀라 뛰쳐나가듯 '도망치다'입니다.

entries.sense_en: a waterproof coat, a raincoat

synonyms.nuance: The everyday word for any coat that keeps out rain.
Short informal British form of mackintosh.
Belted raincoat with a military-style look.
synonyms.example: a detective in a trench coat

entries.tip_ko: 발명가 Charles Macintosh의 이름에서 온 말로, 애플의 Mac과는 관계가 없습니다.

entries.sense_en: to suddenly lose your courage or calm and become frightened
entries.sense_ko: 겁에 질려 평정을 잃다, 용기를 잃다

synonyms.nuance: Informal; decide not to do something because you are afraid.
synonyms.example: He chickened out of the jump.

synonyms.nuance: Sudden wild fear that stops clear thinking.
Become nervous just before a big step such as a wedding.
synonyms.example: She got cold feet before the wedding.

entries.tip_ko: 이 표현에서 nerve는 '신경'이 아니라 '용기, 배짱'이라는 뜻입니다. 'What a nerve!'는 '뻔뻔하기도 하지!'.
